structure: Part 6, Arrival details. Read in full every file of src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/arrival-details/ (page.js, fields.js, controller.js, template.njk, arrival-bounds.js, evaluation.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js and the three test files arrival-bounds.test.js, controller.test.js, copy/copy.test.js, plus arrival-details.fit.spec.js), and for context journeys/linear/features/timing-windows.js, obligations/sections/arrival.js and the parts of src/server/app/shared/kit.js the page uses (pageRoutes, dateField, readDate, base, errorSummary, recoverableSave, nextTarget), src/server/app/shared/paths.js, src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js (saveActions and validatorDefaults), src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/set.js (SET_BASE), features/arrival-status/statuses.js, features/place-of-destination/page.js, fit/set-base.js and the fit harness helpers the spec calls (describeDatePickerLook, expectThreeSaveControls, chooseTypeAheadOption, expectNoSeriousOrCriticalViolations). Covered: the one page at /high-risk-plants/notifications/{journeyId}/arrival-details, its route, caption, heading and save controls; its three fields (arrivalDate always, arrivalTime and proposedPlaceOfLanding for potatoes only) with every label, hint, option text and component; the three date states (potatoes, not-yet-arrived, already-arrived) and the wording each gives; every validation rule and its message in English and machine-draft Welsh; the arrival-bounds today-in-London cap; the stale-port recovery on GET; what the page commits and what it purges when the commodity type changes; the 26 tests of arrival-details.fit.spec.js (the shared describeDatePickerLook block adds four more) and the unit tests of the controller, the bounds helper and the copy. The arrival-status question itself (part 5), the obligation manifest and timing windows (part 12) and the shared kit (part 13) are claimed elsewhere and read here only as context.

claims.statement: The today cap on an already-arrived consignment's date is the calendar day in Europe/London, read from one clock reading, so an entry made at half past midnight British Summer Time can still name that day.
claims.note: mechanism: compares nothing itself — it turns one instant into the latest allowed arrival date, as midnight UTC for the validator and as d/m/yyyy text for the date picker's cap, and returns no bound at all for a consignment that has not arrived.

claims.statement: The page holds a notifier to no notification window: nothing on it refuses a potato notification made fewer than two days before arrival or a plants or wood notification made more than four days after it.
claims.quote:

 * arrival-details validation and the lateness rules all read them from this

claims.note: Looked in arrival-details/controller.js (its imports and its only date rule), arrival-bounds.js and the controller and fit tests: the page imports timing-windows.js nowhere, its only bound is today for an already-arrived consignment, and no test asserts a window. The timing-windows comment says the arrival-details validation reads these figures, which the page does not. The lateness rule is part 10's to claim.
